material.text: opencode-peers: Cross-session messaging for opencode (one package for v1 and v2 hosts) — let independent sessions discover and text each other, modeled after Claude Code's cross-session messaging

# OpenCode Peers **Cross-session messaging for opencode.** [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/opencode-peers)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/opencode-peers) [![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/opencode-peers)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/opencode-peers) ![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%E2%89%A518-339933?logo=nodedotjs&logoColor=white) ![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green)
OpenCode Peers lets independent [opencode](https://opencode.ai) instances on the same machine discover each other and exchange plain-text messages, modeled after [Claude Code's cross-session messaging](https://claudefa.st/blog/guide/mechanics/cross-session-messaging). Run several opencode terminals in parallel (different repos, worktrees, or tasks) and let them hand each other conclusions instead of copy-pasting context between windows — the agent itself decides when to consult a peer, via tools. One package supports both hosts: OpenCode 2.x (v2 plugin API) and opencode >= 1.18.29 (v1 plugin API) — each host picks its own entry. ## ✨ Features - **`list_agents` / `send_message` tools** — the agent discovers peers and texts them. Every message carries a tracking ID, and `peer_message_status` distinguishes transport receipt from final delivery. On OpenCode 2.x the tools are direct model tool calls (not Code Mode catalog entries), matching the v1 host. - **Instant delivery, even while busy** — accepted messages are injected immediately while the target session is busy, as synthetic user messages (`promptAsync` on v1, `ctx.session.synthetic` on v2), one host call per message. The sender keeps a pending final ACK until delivery completes. - **One endpoint per session** — including child sessions. Exact endpoint IDs disambiguate duplicate names. - **Durable by default** — per-session queues, held messages, delivery outcomes, and sender outboxes survive process restarts. - **Inbound gating** — `accept` / `auto` / `hold` / `refuse`. `auto` accepts same-directory peers and holds cross-directory messages. - **Unattended peer turns** — permission requests raised while acting on an injected peer message are auto-approved, scoped as described in [Security](#-security). Your own turns are unaffected. - **Inline results** — command output and notifications land in the session, no toast popups. - **TUI controls** — palette actions with host dialogs on OpenCode 2.x and single-Enter slash commands on both hosts. - **Plain text only** — no files, no shared conversation history. - **Local only** — Unix-domain sockets on macOS/Linux, loopback TCP on Windows. Everything stays on your machine. ## ⌨️ Commands | Command | What it does | | --- | --- | | `/peers` (alias `/list-agents`) | List other opencode sessions: state, name, directory, uptime | | `/peers-name ` | Name this instance so peers can address it | | `/peers-inbox` | List held messages. `accept ` / `drop all` | | `/peers-outbox` | Receipts and final ACK outcomes | Default peer name is `-` (e.g. `my-app-a3f2`), so same-directory instances stay distinguishable. `/peers-name` or the `name` option replaces it. ## ⚙️ Settings Register the plugin in config by package name — `plugins` on OpenCode 2.x, the singular `plugin` key on v1 — and carry options in the object/tuple form: ```json { "plugins": ["opencode-peers"] } { "plugin": ["opencode-peers"] } { "plugins": [ { "package": "opencode-peers", "options": { "inboundPolicy": "hold", "name": "frontend" } } ] } { "plugin": [ [ "opencode-peers", { "inboundPolicy": "hold", "name": "frontend" } ] ] } ``` | Option | Default | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | | `inboundPolicy` | `"accept"` | `accept` delivers immediately. `auto` accepts only when sender and receiver directories match and otherwise holds. `hold` parks messages for review. `refuse` rejects them | | `peerPermissions` | `"allow"` | Peer-origin permission requests: `allow` auto-approves ordinary requests, `ask` leaves native prompts untouched, `deny` rejects. Even in `allow`, permission configuration, `AGENTS.md`, credentials/secrets and escalation are never auto-approved. Existing deny rules always win | | `name` | `-` | Display name other peers use to address you | | `storageDir` | `$XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode-peers` | Where the registry and held inbox live | | `heartbeatMs` | `10000` | Registry heartbeat interval | | `staleMs` | `60000` | Peer is offline if its heartbeat is older than this | | `maxQueue` | `50` | Queued (accepted, undelivered) message cap | | `maxHeld` | `100` | Held inbox cap | | `heldExpiryMs` | `300000` | Held approval expiry. Expiry produces a final ACK | | `maxMessageBytes` | `8192` | Per-message size cap | | `sendRatePerMin` | `10` | Outbound rate limit per peer | | `recvRatePerMin` | `20` | Inbound rate limit per sender | | `sweepMs` | `15000` | Fallback delivery/ACK reliability sweep interval | ## 📦 Install One package, two hosts — pick your host's command: ```bash opencode plugin add opencode-peers # OpenCode 2.x (v2) opencode plugin -g opencode-peers # opencode v1 (>= 1.18.29) ``` Config-based registration and options live in the Settings section below. Development checkout: ```bash git clone https://github.com/chinese-room-solutions/opencode-peers cd opencode-peers && make build ``` ```jsonc // ~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc { "plugins": ["/abs/path/to/opencode-peers"] } ``` Point v2 hosts at the package directory, never `dist/index.js`. On v1, symlink instead: `ln -sf "$PWD/dist/index.js" ~/.config/opencode/plugins/opencode-peers.js`. ## 🔒 Security - **Same-machine trust**: any process running as your user can read the registry files and therefore talk to your instances' inboxes. The bearer token protects against other users and accidental connections, not against a malicious process with your UID. - **Prompt injection**: a peer message is untrusted input to the model, exactly like pasted text. Plain text cannot transfer files, history, consent, or executable commands. - **Auto-allow is trust, not a boundary**: the `peerPermissions: "allow"` default withholds auto-approval for requests that *mention* sensitive paths (permission config, `AGENTS.md`, credentials, shell startup files), but the guard matches on request text — a cleverly phrased request can dodge it. Treat `allow` as fully trusting every peer on the machine. Use `ask`, `hold`, or `refuse` when it isn't. - Auto-allow only ever replies to turns started by a message the plugin injected. Requests from your own typed turns fall through to opencode's normal flow untouched. ## 🔧 How it works ``` OpenCode process A OpenCode process B ┌──────────────────────────────┐ ┌──────────────────────────────┐ │ session A1 → endpoint/spool │ │ session B1 → endpoint/spool │ │ session A2 → endpoint/spool │ │ session B2 → endpoint/spool │ │ durable outbox ◄─────────────├─final ACK─┤ local UDS/TCP listener │ │ registry v1 + v2 ────────────┼──────────►│ promptAsync(exact session) │ └──────────────────────────────┘ └──────────────────────────────┘ ``` Discovery publishes one registry record per live session endpoint (a closed process disappears within one stale window). HTTP acceptance is only a receipt — final `delivered` / `refused` / `expired` / `dropped` / `duplicate` ACKs are durably retried to the sender. Messages carry a `via` hop list. Chains longer than 4 hops are rejected. ## 🛠️ Development ```bash make build # compile (tsc → dist/) make watch # recompile on change (auto-installs deps on first run) make typecheck # type-check without emitting make test # build + full node --test suite make package # build + npm pack ``` ### Tests The suite includes real-host integration tests that spawn actual `opencode serve` processes: `tests/real-opencode.test.mjs` needs an opencode v1 binary, `tests/real-opencode-v2.test.mjs` an opencode v2 binary — each skips with a message when its host isn't on PATH. CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs the suite on Linux twice — once against a pinned opencode v1 host, once against a pinned v2 host. Pushing a version tag (e.g. `v0.1.0`, matching `package.json`) builds the tarball and publishes a GitHub release with it (`.github/workflows/release.yml`). ## Credits This project is a standalone continuation of [opencode-plugin-peers](https://github.com/jkrandom-sudo/opencode-plugin-peers), forked at v0.2.3 and extended with OpenCode v2 support, event-driven discovery, synthetic delivery, and evaluate-hook permissions. The original project is MIT-licensed. Its copyright notice is preserved in the [LICENSE](./LICENSE) file as its license requires.
